sections.fullText: While packing for relocation, I discovered a huge pile of items that were no longer needed. Clothes, old toys the kids used to play with, board games, puzzles and a few furniture items like chairs and a work desk.
I tried my best to find some use to al these items but honestly, with all the hassle of packing and leaving the apartment I was in, giving them away seemed to be the best option.

I thought about the underprivileged children living in foundation homes around the city and quickly realised that giving all my old clothing items, toys and furniture to them would be a much better option than just throwing them away.

The next task in front of me was locating a good NGO near me, that provided enough information on how my old items can be used and where they are headed. I was determined to make sure my old items won’t end up in the dump yard.

A quick google search led me to SevaDeep, an initiative by Pune’s Relfor Foundation, that bridges the gap between donors and NGOs. The digital platform lists thousands of NGOs around the country, their contact details, their area of work and the current requirements. I was happy to see that the platform only accepted donations of old appliances, furniture, clothes, toys, without engaging in monetary donations. The platform also authenticates each and every NGO.

After scrolling through for a few minutes, I came across Shree Santraj Yogi Shikshan Sanstha. According to the SevaDeep platform, the foundation provides a safe home for children of single parents, who cannot support themselves. This looked like a good match for me. I clicked the donate button and after filling a few details, I received a confirmation and a scheduled time for pick up of my donation (this was an extremely pleasant surprise).

The SevaDeep truck arrived a few minutes before the scheduled time, and the driver examined my items. After verifying that they were indeed usable, he packed them on the truck and informed me that he was going to the item storage and that within a day or two, all my items will be delivered to the NGO.

The entire experience was absolutely flawless. The entire process, from the decision to donate the items to their pickup by the SevaDeep team, didn’t take more than a couple of hours, and I had no hassles.
The kind SevaDeep representative just asked me to sign my pickup note and refused to accept the tip I offered.

It’s been a couple of months since I made my first donation to the NGO near me through SevaDeep. Although I have settled in my new apartment, I can tell you that I constantly look for items to donate to the NGOs that they list on the platform.
The initiative is the need of the hour, especially now that these wonderful volunteers, the foundations and the people they serve face acute shortages due to the lockdown and tough weather.

I urge you all to visit their website and schedule a donation of your old items today! Don’t forget to follow them on Facebook for more news. A big shout out to their team for the great service and initiative.
